restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes, so the single padded block ends in 0x86; c+p = 520 initial-state bits are fixed. Complete fixed-zero-state SHA3-256 sponge with 0x06 suffix and prefix rounds 0 through 4, as in verifier/keccak.py:sha3_256(data, 5).
Two hash-collision-witness-v2 certificates (collision-a, collision-b) are the verified outputs of the executed program; correctness rests on the organizer verifier, not on the proof.

The claim concerns one fixed deterministic program (fixed seeds, caps and thresholds; no algorithmic coins) that was executed in full. Success probability 1 refers to this program; it is not an expected-cost claim for fresh seeds (context in proof Section 9).

Charged time is the measured CPU time of all work that produced the pairs, including the trail search, aborted, exploratory and development runs, replay and verification: at most 58.2 core-hours (rusage, or threads x wall time where rusage was lost, plus two bounded estimates). It is charged as a 128 core-hour budget at 2^48 primitives per core-hour and 1/1355 unit per primitive, plus 1 unit per full five-round evaluation.
The trail core is not hard-coded: a blind, capped search with GLL+20's published thresholds (App. C.2) recovered GLL+20 trail core No. 3 as the unique minimum-w1 core; the search is charged.

The connector is GLL+20's 2-round linearized connector with changes required for 8 fixed padding bits (path-aware difference phase, interleaved value phase, #AS(alpha1) hill-climb, exact implied-hull preProcess); the paper's literal procedure fails for p = 8.
The published 1084-bit GLL+20 pair is outside the byte-string domain and is used only as validation evidence.
Supersedes our earlier heuristic package for this track (time_log2 56.35, no certificate), whose literal connector step does not work as written.
The nominal reference identifier does not itself assert an improvement.

heuristics.statement: One CPU core-hour of the executed binaries on the Apple M4 Pro used performs at most 2^48 v5 primitive 256-bit word operations, so the charged 128 core-hours correspond to at most 2^55 primitives, i.e. 2^44.596 units at 1/1355 unit per primitive.
heuristics.scope: Conversion of measured CPU time (rusage, or threads x wall time where rusage was lost) into collision-frontier-v5 primitives for every charged item of proof Section 7.1. Full five-round evaluations are additionally charged 1 unit each (< 2^18 units).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware counters were recorded for three runs covering every code path (connector + brute force, trail stage A, trail stages B/C): 1.21e10 to 1.40e10 instructions retired per CPU-second. With at most 3 primitives per AArch64 instruction this is at most 4.2e10 primitives per second = 2^47.1 per core-hour. About 90% of the charged CPU time (the other runs of the same binaries and workloads) is extrapolated from these rates.
heuristics.limitations: Instruction counters were not recorded for the largest run (run A, charged at its 13-thread x wall upper bound) or for development runs; their rates are inferred from the same code on the same machine. The at-most-3-primitives-per-instruction mapping is an argument about AArch64 instruction semantics, not a measurement. The ceiling is 1.9x above the highest measured rate, and the 2.2x budget margin is separate.

heuristics.statement: The unlogged development and diagnostic work (connector tests, analyses and simulations: at most 4 core-hours; exploratory trail work: at most 4 core-hours, itemized at about 2.9; verification: at most 0.1 core-hours) is within the stated bounds.
heuristics.scope: Three of the ten rows of the proof Section 7.1 cost table, 14% of the 58.2 core-hour total.
heuristics.extrapolation: The bounds are reconstructed from logged command lines, short fixed-duration test runs (20 to 60 s each) and partial rusage; they are not complete rusage records.
heuristics.limitations: Some short development runs were not individually timed. The 2.2x budget margin (128 versus 58.2 core-hours) absorbs these items even if they were about 9 times larger, so an error here does not change time_log2.
